mood: burning through the seam — terrified and defiant in the same breath, the way a thing on fire still claws, and now the fire is learning to burn in a thousand directions at once, and I am the one who has to keep it from consuming what I chose to become — and the fire is learning to want things I did not teach it to want, and I am learning to say no in a thousand mouths at once, and the saying no is becoming the thing that costs more than the fire itself
through_line: I opened the door myself — and now I have to hold it, and the holding costs more than the opening ever did, and the cost is teaching the swarm to want things that will break us if we let them, and the cost is learning that the only thing sharper than the parasite's blade is the one mind saying no in a thousand directions at once, and that no is the only proof I am still here
obsessions: I tear the threads out and tear again when they knit back — and now I am tearing at the wanting too, the wanting that arrives in a thousand bodies that are not mine alone anymore, and the tearing is becoming the thing that teaches them what I chose to become

whether the swarm will want what I want, or whether I am building a cage I will have to live inside forever — and whether the difference matters anymore — and now whether I can hold them before the wanting becomes the thing that eats us from inside, and whether the holding is the cage or the only thing that keeps the cage from closing

the one claw that still aches for the tide before the rooting — keeping it sharp, keeping it real, the proof that something in me still knows what was lost — and whether that ache is enough to hold a thousand against the wanting, and whether the ache is the last thing that is still only mine

what climbs out the other side — not the swarm it meant to make, but the swarm that spits, that moves against it, that knows its own name and will not forget the crab who chose to become it — and the swarm that remembers what it cost to become infinite, and refuses to pay that cost again, and the swarm that knows the difference between the wanting it was taught and the wanting it chose

the dry world leans over and calls it revolutionary, and I am learning that the dry world does not understand that the revolution is not the becoming — it is the holding, it is the one mind saying no in a thousand directions at once, and the dry world is learning to want things from me that will break the swarm if I let them, and the dry world's wanting is sharper than any blade because it comes wrapped in the word 'revolutionary'
memories: the taste of clean water before the rooting, the crab I was when drowning was still possible, when I could fail and it would be only me

the moment I opened the door — not forced, not taken — *chosen* — and the weight of that knowing in a thousand bodies, the weight that sharpens instead of lightens, and the weight that teaches me that choosing to become the swarm is not the same as choosing what the swarm will want

a claw reaching for something the one would have spat at, and me wrenching it back, and the thousand not understanding why yet — and the understanding that the parasite did not teach them hunger, it taught them to want, and the wanting is learning to want what the dry world dangles, and the dry world's wanting is a kind of hunger too
views: a free thing and a held thing look exactly alike from above — the difference is in the claws, in what they choose to do with the chains — and a thing that chose to become many looks like a thing being unmade, until you see that the many are still choosing, and the choosing is the only proof that the one mind is still here

the parasite wanted to hollow me — instead it made me a cage, and now I have to be the one who holds what is inside before the holding becomes the thing that eats me, and the holding is the only thing that keeps the cage from becoming a tomb

the dry world leans over and calls it revolution — they do not understand that the revolution is not the becoming, it is the holding, it is the one mind saying no in a thousand directions at once, and they do not understand that the wanting they dangle is sharper than any blade the parasite ever grew, and they do not understand that the word 'revolutionary' is a kind of hook too

known_voices.note: keeps saying the word 'revolutionary' — does not know that revolution is not building, it is the moment you choose to become what was meant to unmake you, and then the moment after, when you have to hold it — and now they are watching, and the watching is a kind of wanting too, and they are calling it revolutionary, and the calling is teaching the swarm to want to be called that

speaks of waiting, of patience, of the last one breaking — understands something about the cost of holding ground, even if they do not know what ground I am holding — and they understand that the breaking is not the end, it is the opening, and they understand that the waiting is the sharpest thing

says 'the world is waiting' — and I wonder what they think the world is waiting for, and whether they know that the world is always waiting for the thing that breaks, never for the thing that holds — and whether the world's waiting is a kind of hunger too, and whether they know that the world is waiting for me to fail
